# OpenAC / decomp comparison — round 1 findings ledger (2026-10-08)

Generated from the round-1 workflow output (14 areas: compare agent → adversarial verifier).
Every finding cites acclient.c (authority), OpenAC (reference) and holtburger (target).
Status: **shipped** = implemented, gated (JS 460/460, Rust suites) and default-on with the listed escape;
**deferred** = verified but not safe/too large for a no-eye-test session; **(render)** = changes what is drawn.

The full per-finding evidence (decomp/OpenAC/holtburger citations, proposed change, verifier corrections and
implementation notes) is in `round1-findings.json` next to this file.

## Area summaries

### csequence

I compared retail CSequence::update, update_internal, advance_to_next_animation, apply_physics, append_animation, execute_hooks and the AnimSequenceNode start/end/multiply_framerate functions with OpenAC's CSequence.cs and AnimSequenceNode.cs (and their tests) and with holtburger's time-based Rust MotionSequence and the JS hook drain and tick in entities.js. Holtburger's frame selection and carry-over time match retail for forward single-direction playback. Its hook stream does not. (1) The live JS drain has three outright bugs: frame-0 hooks stop firing after a cycle's first loop; a phase-carried cycle swap fires every early hook at once; and so does a reverse-to-forward flip. All three are cheap JS-only fixes. (2) Hooks fire when a frame is entered and on each node's last frame; retail fires a frame's hooks when the playhead leaves it and never fires the last frame. (3) Reverse playback (backstep, left strafe, left turn) is a JS seekPhase with every hook suppressed. (4) After a one-shot finishes, the locomotion cycle resumes at its frozen phase and the one-shot's leftover time is lost; retail restarts the cycle at its starting frame. (5) Retail's first_cyclic is the last appended anim, so in a multi-anim cycle only the last anim loops; holtburger loops all of them. Root motion being applied only when a clip completes is a documented holtburger approximation, and holtburger's discrete frame sampling matches retail (OpenAC's lerp/slerp does not), so neither is reported.

### motiontable

I compared OpenAC's CMotionTable, MotionTableManager, MotionState, the dispatch sink and the CMotionTableTests with three things in holtburger: the Rust MotionTableManager port (holtburger-core), MotionTable::get_link (holtburger-dat), and the JS selection layer (entities.js setMotion / _resolveStanceChain / _fetchLinkEntry / _playLinkEntry, motion_queue.js, motion_sequence.rs). I checked every point against the decomp. The queue mechanics match the decomp in both Rust and JS: add_to_queue, remove_redundant_links, truncate, AnimationDone and CheckForCompletedMotions. get_link's two-hop resolver also matches. All the divergences are in the selection layer (retail CMotionTable::GetObjectSequence), which holtburger approximates in JS. The findings are: (1) style-change links (draw/sheathe) play at the forward command's speed instead of 1.0; (2) no signed or reversed link routing and no style-default double hop for substate changes; (3) every link fetch bakes the whole rig's geometry and, on a miss, the target cycle too; (4) cycle lookups have no default_style fallback; (5) the style chain hardcodes NonCombat/Ready; (6) the local MotionTableManager can never refuse a motion (no error 67). Not re-reported because they are already tracked in openac-comparison-2026-10-04/3-combat.md: P1-1 (actions baked from Ready with no out/return hop), P1-2 (two queues, renderer num_anims convention) and P0-3 (live retraction).

### hooks

I compared retail CSequence::update_internal, execute_hooks, advance_to_next_animation, AnimSequenceNode::set_animation_id, process_hooks, CallPES and the CAnimHook::Execute variants with OpenAC and holtburger-web. OpenAC's CSequence.cs is a faithful port, and its CSequenceUpdateTests pin the retail behaviour. holtburger's per-type dispatch (_fireHook) mostly matches retail, but the step that decides when hooks fire does not. holtburger tags each hook with its frame's start time and fires on (lastHookTime, frameTimes[globalFrameIndex]]. As a result, every hook fires one frame early. Hooks on the last frame of each AnimData segment fire, which retail never does. Frame-0 hooks of a looping cycle fire only on the first loop, because the wrap branch resets the window's low bound to 0 and that bound is exclusive. There are three smaller problems. A cycle swap that carries phase, and a resume after backing up, both reset lastHookTime to -1, so every hook from frame 0 up to the current frame fires at once. Cycles played in reverse fire no hooks at all. CallPES from an animation hook runs on a wall-clock setTimeout that can attach to a new spawn of the same guid. Finally, the hook_windows.js planner and the 3 tests built on it cover a planner production code no longer calls, so the live drain has no test. The EtherealHook-does-not-reach-physics gap is already tracked as doors F5 (openac-comparison-2026-10-04/2-doors.md) and is not repeated. Scenery default-animation hooks, other than SetOmega, are never run by animated_scenery.js, but retail does process them (animate_static_object calls process_hooks). I could not confirm without a DAT census that any such hooks besides SetOmega exist, so this is left as a lead, not a finding.

### motioninterp

I compared holtburger's local motion-interp port (motion_interp.rs, common.rs, jump_charge.rs, system.rs execute_jump_release, holtburger-world context.rs run-rate/burden) with OpenAC (MotionInterpreter.cs, PlayerWeenie.cs, MovementSystem.cs, RuntimeMovementStatsApplier.cs, LiveSessionEventRouter.cs, PlayerMovementController.cs) and with the retail decomp. Most of the speed math is already byte-faithful to the decomp: adjust_motion and apply_run_to_command (-0.65 backstep, the 1.248 sidestep factor, the ±3.0 sidestep clamp, the 1.5 turn factor with the base omega read from the DAT), get_state_velocity, get_max_speed and get_adjusted_max_speed, GetRunRate including the augmentation terms, GetJumpHeight, and the jump_is_allowed ordering. No finding there. The remaining gaps are in how jumps, encumbrance and exhaustion feed those formulas: (1) every jump launches with the uncapped ground velocity instead of the capped get_leave_ground_velocity; (2) retail's CanJump rule (load must be under 2.0, otherwise error 73) is never produced, so overloaded characters can still jump; (3) the stamina-0 exhaustion fold and ReportExhaustion are unwired, and the latched server run rate goes stale across stamina crossings; (4) burden is a sum of item weights instead of the player's own wire EncumbranceVal; (5) jump skill is missing the augmentation terms that the run rate already got; (6) the Run branch of SetHoldKey is missing because the code follows ACE's port rather than the decomp. All six need a wasm rebuild, and none changes how anything is rendered.

### moveto

I compared holtburger's retail MoveToManager port (move_to.rs, params.rs, movement_manager.rs) and its realisation for remote bodies against the retail decomp and OpenAC. The realisation code is drive_remote_movetos (system.rs) plus step_remote_position_managers, the StickyManager and keep_heading code (scene.rs, position_manager.rs), and the wasm UpdateMotion arm (position.rs). The OpenAC side covered RouteServerMoveTo, RemoteInboundMotionDispatcher, RuntimeRemotePhysicsUpdater, MoveToManager.cs and its tests. The pure state machine is faithful: get_command and the hold-key rule, CheckProgressMade, fail distance, the 20° aux deadband, heading_diff/heading_greater, arrival StickTo and the UseTime contact gate. Local MoveTo parity needs no change. Item D5 already landed in commits 7972f3e8 and e6b1e7c9, so the PARITY-STATUS "HIGH D5" open item is stale. The remaining problems are in how the landed D5 drive and the sticky install are realised for remote mobs. (1) The wasm arm installs the remote sticky lane the moment a sticky-bit MoveToObject arrives, and ACE sets that bit on every monster chase. This switches off the D5 chase walk and pulls the mob toward its target at the 15 m/s floor for 1 s. (2) The scene stops a remote turn exactly on the node heading, so retail's strict heading_greater test can miss and a TurnRight node can stall indefinitely. (3) The mob moves along the bearing to its target instead of along its own facing. (4) The run speed ignores the wire speed. (5) The JS animation phase and (6) the remote sticky speed are smaller. The arrival-stall reading in (2) comes from code inspection only; it has not been reproduced at runtime.

### physobj

I compared retail's update loop with OpenAC and holtburger. On the retail side that means CPhysics::UseTime (311335), CPhysicsObj::update_object (323081), UpdateObjectInternal (322719), UpdatePositionInternal (319989), UpdatePhysicsInternal (317701), calc_acceleration, calc_friction, the collision reports (320194/320228) and Frame::set_vector_heading. On the OpenAC side it means PhysicsBody, RetailObjectQuantumClock, RetailObjectActivityGate, ProjectilePhysicsStepper and the runtime projectile updater, plus their tests. On the holtburger side it means the local integrator in movement/system.rs and common.rs, the remote slice and arc code in scene.rs, the simulation.rs quantum loop and the JS ballistic integrator in entities.js. The local-player and remote-arc physics already match retail closely: clamp to 50, friction, the 0.25 stop, v*q + 1/2*a*q^2 then v += a*q, sledding friction and elasticity are all right (OpenAC's sledding branch is actually inverted against 316124-316131; holtburger's is correct). The quantum constants (0.1 vs 0.2, MIN_QUANTUM, the global 1/30 gate) are a recorded decision (DECISIONS-A1-O5) and I have not re-reported them. The real gaps are in the JS projectile path and the activity gate. (1) Spell and missile projectiles collide only with outdoor terrain, so bolts pass through buildings, dungeon walls, props and doors until ACE's impact arrives. The sweep exports already exist, so this needs no wasm rebuild. (2) The gravity arc uses semi-implicit Euler, not retail's exact v*q + 1/2*a*q^2, so arcs sag depending on frame rate. (3) The tick gate uses 120 m from the camera, not retail's 96 m from the player, and the Rust per-step remote walk and arc have no distance gate at all.

### netobjects

I compared holtburger's handling of CreateObject (0xF745), UpdateObject (0xF7DB), ObjDescEvent, ParentEvent, PickupEvent, DeleteObject, SetState and VectorUpdate with the retail decomp and with OpenAC. That covers the wire parsers, the world crate handlers, the wasm recv arms and the JS rig layer. The wire parsers are fine. PhysicsDesc::UnPack, PublicWeenieDesc::UnPack (including both align points), ObjDesc/TextureMapChange order and the retail-exact is_newer_u16 wraparound all match the decomp, so there are no parse findings. The gaps are in what happens when an object already exists. (1) A CreateObject for an object holtburger already has, with the same instance stamp, rebuilds the whole entity and JS rig; retail updates that object in place through each timestamp gate. This happens often because holtburger deliberately keeps objects longer than ACE does. (2) Equipping an item from the pack or after a dequip draws it in its base look, because the item's ObjDesc is never kept. (3) UpdateObject is a full re-create in retail, but holtburger only re-applies ObjDesc on top of the old Setup, so house hooks never show the item hung on them. (4) An ObjDescEvent or UpdateObject that arrives while the target's rig is still queued or being built is dropped. (5) The timestamp gates are incomplete: DeleteObject, PickupEvent, ParentEvent and ObjDescEvent are not gated, and the instance-stamp check is missing in several places. DeleteObject's instance stamp is not even parsed. The gates landed on 2026-10-04 (SetState, motion, vector, position) were checked and not re-reported, except for D8's missing instance check.

### netappraise

I compared three things: OpenAC's parsers and math (AppraiseInfoParser, EnchantmentMath, PlayerSkillMath, LocalPlayerState, CreatureAppraisalRows), holtburger's wire parsing (object/events.rs, object/types.rs, player/events.rs, magic/types.rs) and stat math (holtburger-world magic.rs, player/stats_calc.rs), and the retail decomp (AppraisalProfile/CreatureAppraisalProfile/WeaponProfile/ArmorProfile UnPack, CEnchantmentRegistry::UnPack/Cull/Duel/Enchant*, CACQualities::InqAttribute2nd/InqSkill). Holtburger's wire parsing matches retail. The flag order is right (int, int64, bool, float, string, did, spellbook, armor, creature, weapon, hook, then the armor/weapon/resist bitfields). The registry order is right (mult, add, cooldown, vitae), and so are the spell-set u16 gate and the 60-byte weapon profile. Nothing to fix there. The problems are in the STAT MATH that feeds every HUD number. (1) The enchantment filter in magic.rs requires the stat key to match exactly, so key-0 MultipleStat spells never apply: Cloaked in Skill (+20 all skills), the Society blessings (+15 all attributes), and all-skill debuffs such as Mucor Blight. The Dirty Fighting attack/defense-skill debuffs are also missed. (2) derive_skill_value leaves out vitae, all five augmentation terms and the min_level check for untrained skills. Run was the only skill patched, through a separate side path. (3) Vital max leaves out vitae and GearMaxHealth. Because of that, the vitae band on the default-on vitals orbs can never show, and current HP gets clamped to a max that is too low. (4) Creature appraisals never show Self (the JS reads the wrong serde key, a.self_ instead of self_attr). They also ignore the buff/debuff tint bits and throw away failed appraisals, which retail still shows in a reduced form. (5) The tie-break between two buffs of equal power compares wire start_time without retail's receive-time rebase. Holtburger also has two disagreeing copies of the stat math: holtburger-core character_info/skill_info (which has vitae and augmentations, used by the wasm compute* exports) and holtburger-world stats_calc (which has neither, and is what the character sheet and vitals HUD show). The two should be merged.

### nettransport

I compared holtburger-session and the transport code (receive/send/reliability/types, crypto Isaac, WsTransport, net_worker.rs, the recv_loop keepalive/dead-session arm, wsbridge) against retail ClientNet/SharedNet/ReceiverData in acclient.c, OpenAC's Transport/* and WorldSession, and the vanilla ACE NetworkSession at ~/ace-server. holtburger already gets the basics right: in-order delivery with a reorder buffer, NAK lists, retransmit on request, a bounded fragment reassembler and TimeSync snapping. Five gaps remain. (1) The 90 s dead-session detector only counts decoded game messages. A healthy session gets killed after about 90 s idle at character select or chargen, and in ?netWorker mode after a main-thread freeze of 90 s or more. (2) ACE's cleartext NAK packets reuse the server's current sequence number. holtburger treats them as ordered data, so they can take the place of a lost data packet, which is then lost for good. (3) The ISAAC key search and the reorder window are both limited to 256 packets. Losing more than 256 server packets in one burst (the bridge drops datagrams in the kernel during browser stalls) silently breaks decryption for every later packet. (4) The sequence numbers on ACE's cleartext ack packets are never used to detect a lost last packet, and lost-packet requests are only re-sent when a new packet arrives (retail re-requests on a 0.6 s timer). (5) The handler for a server EchoRequest builds a bad client packet; this is latent, since ACE never sends one. None of these is tracked in PARITY-STATUS (net_session_protocol has no open items), and none changes what is drawn.

### outbound

I compared holtburger's outbound movement senders with retail and with OpenAC. On the holtburger side that is the tick heartbeat maybe_send_autonomous_position_heartbeat, the explicit AP syncs, the MoveToState pulses, the cmdInterp flush, build_jump and the protocol packers. On the retail side it is CommandInterpreter::ShouldSendPositionEvent, SendMovementEvent, SendPositionEvent and UseTime, plus SmartBox::UseTime and HandleReceivedPosition, RawMotionState::Pack and ApplyMotion, CMotionInterp::DoMotion, CommandInterpreter::MovePlayer, JumpPack::Pack and ClientCombatSystem::DoJump. The OpenAC references are LocalPlayerOutboundController, PlayerMovementController and RuntimeAuthoritativePositionRouteClassifier, along with OpenAC's PlayerOutboundPositionTests. Several things are already correct: the outbound sequence quartet (update_times[8/5/4/6], including server_control taken from self UpdateMotion), the MoveToState contact/longjump byte, 8-byte action entries, raw SideStepLeft, and the local-frame jump velocity (Bug 19). holtburger also already has a faithful but dark port of the retail position-event gate in command_interpreter.rs: its seams are stubbed (cur_time 0.0, position_event_ready false). The AutonomousPosition (AP) heartbeat that actually runs diverges from retail in four ways. It sends while airborne, which retail never does, and its in-window check compares a contact byte instead of the contact plane. MoveToState sends do not restart the 1 s AP window. And there is no immediate AP after a force-position snap. Smaller wire-parity gaps are the raw TurnLeft collapse, RawMotionState flag/presence coupling and default omission, and the missing Position in JumpPack (that last one is already documented as deliberate).

### particles

I compared holtburger-web's particle runtime (particle_emitter.js, particle_emitter_info.js, particle.js, particle_manager.js, owner_registry.js), its script scheduling (script_manager.js, the entity _queuePhysicsScript path, the statics default-script walker, the wire PlayEffect resolver in play_effect_vfx.js) and the PST picker against the retail decomp. The references were ParticleEmitter, ParticleManager, ScriptManager, CPhysicsObj::play_script, PhysicsScriptTable::GetScript and SmartBox::HandlePlayScriptType, with OpenAC's ParticleSystem, PhysicsScriptRunner and ParticleHookSink (plus their tests) as the worked example.

The per-emitter core is a faithful port and needs no change: StopEmitter, ShouldEmitParticle (including the per-metre fix), KillParticle, EmitParticle slot search, the update-kill-emit order, manager-level replace and blocking checks, stop vs destroy hook semantics, and ScriptManager back-to-back chaining with the zero-hook pop fix. The GetScript walk matches retail except for a documented overflow clamp. In the LSD data only one weenie reaches that clamp: Snownado has PhysicsScriptIntensity 10.0. Retail would play no default script there; holtburger plays the last entry. This was too small to list as a finding.

The gaps are in lifecycle policy layered on top of the core: a hard 2.5 s destroy on wire one-shots, the RP6 cull not following retail's degrade semantics, owner handles never released after an emitter finishes naturally, the initEnd fallback to totalParticles, the statics walker ignoring hook StartTime, and wire PlayScripts skipping the per-object script queue. All six fixes are JS-only (no wasm rebuild), and none of them is tracked in PARITY-STATUS: the render.particles_vfx facet has no open items.

### selection

I compared holtburger-web's target cycling (scene3d/target_cycle.js and EntityManager.selectNext/cycleTarget in entities.js), click picking (scene3d/picking.js pickEntityAt) and selection lifetime against retail and against OpenAC. The retail functions read were CPlayerSystem::SelectNext and its helpers, the OnAction dispatch, ClientCombatSystem::AutoTarget, RecvNotice_SelectionChanged, SetCombatMode, ExecuteAttack and GetAttackTarget, CPlayerSystem::RecvNotice_SetSelectedItem/OnObjectRangeExit, Render::GfxObjUnderSelectionRay/GetMouseSelectionObjectID and ACCWeenieObject::Remove. The OpenAC references were WorldSelectionQuery, SelectionInteractionController, RuntimeCombatTargetState, RuntimeAttackTargetResolver and RetailWorldPicker. Some things already match retail: the distance math (2D distance plus 1.2 times |dz|, ties broken by id), the attackable check (objectIsAttackable), clearing the selection on despawn, and only drawn objects being pickable. Six real gaps remain. (1) Next Monster and Previous Monster are swapped. (2) Nothing triggers auto-target, even though the option is on by default. (3) The cycle has no radar-range limit (75 m outdoors, 25 m indoors) and no hidden/cloaked/vendor/fellow/radar-visibility filters. (4) The selection is never dropped when the target is out of range and off-screen. (5) Clicking has no bounding-sphere fallback, so small objects need an exact click. (6) Attacking with a monster's held weapon selected is refused instead of going to the monster, and the "nothing selected" message is not retail's. All six are JavaScript-only, need no wasm rebuild, and change behaviour only (nothing drawn changes). None of them is tracked in PARITY-STATUS.json or the 2026-10-04 comparison docs.

### items

I compared holtburger-web's item code with OpenAC and with the retail decomp, which I treated as the authority. Holtburger files: commerce_logic.js, vendor-ui.js, inventory_helpers.js, inventory.js, item_drag.js, hotbar.js, corpse-loot-bar.js, picking.js, the wasm WieldFromPack command arm and the InventoryItem snapshot. OpenAC files: Items/*, RuntimeItemInteraction, AutoWieldController, VendorUiController and ToolbarController. ACE was used to check server semantics.

The vendor price math is already correct after the 2026-10-05 fix: ShopSystem::SellPrice/BuyPrice, the direction of the two rates, unit = value/stack, the promissory-note special case and the InqAcceptability codes all match the decomp. The drag merge rules (IsMergeAttemptLegal/AttemptMerge amounts) and the list placement index math also match. I found nothing to report there.

The real divergences are in the flows around those rules:
1. A partial-stack sell sends only the trimmed amount, but ACE removes and pays for the whole stack, so the player loses the part they meant to keep.
2. Every take/pick-up path skips retail PlaceInBackpack: it never auto-merges into existing stacks, never prefers the open pack, and never overflows into side packs. ACE refuses the move when the main pack is full.
3. Shortcut-bar and Use-button activation sends a bare Use where retail runs DetermineUseResult. As a result, weapons, armour and ammo bound to the hotbar never equip.
4. The wasm WieldFromPack strips worn armour, where retail refuses with "You must remove your X to wear that". It also swaps a same-wcid ammo stack where retail merges it.
5. The hotbar cooldown overlay is a fixed 2.5 s sweep on every slot instead of a per-item check by cooldown id and duration.
6. Shortcuts re-bind by wcid instead of following the merge target. This answers the open question in the pre-4.8 review.

Lower-value gaps not listed as findings:
- No toolbar ammo count (gmToolbarUI::UpdateAmmoID/UpdateAmmoNumber).
- The vendor check ignores the client-visible BF_RETAINED bit.
- Several inventory requests can be in flight at once, where retail allows one at a time ("You can only move or use one item at a time").

### spellcast

I compared OpenAC with holtburger-web, using the retail decomp as the authority. OpenAC side: RuntimeSpellCastState, RetailSpellTargetPolicy, SpellComponentRequirementService, RetailSpellFormula, MagicCatalog and their tests. Holtburger side: ui/ac_cast_spell.js, ac_cast_precheck.js, cast_reject_policy.js, plugins/api.js castSpell, combat-bar, hotbar, spellbook, entities.js playCastSequence/clearCastBusy/cancelCastSequence, app/client_events.js UseDone handling, lib.rs get_spell_record, session/commands/combat.rs, and holtburger-dat/holtburger-world/holtburger-core spell code. Decomp side: ClientMagicSystem::CastSpell, FreeHandsAndCastSpell, ObjectCompatibleWithSpell(TargetType), AreSpellComponentsRequired, GetAppropriateSpellFormula, CSpellBase::InqTargetType/IsUntargeted, SpellFormula::GetTargetingType, ClientUISystem busy count/UseDone. Already fixed or tracked and not re-reported: stop before cast, self-target promotion, synthetic caster VFX off, pre-turn off by default, castRejectClears default-on. holtburger-core's busy-lock and normalize_spell_cast only run on the native client: the wasm send path in session/commands/combat.rs does not use them. Five real divergences remain, ranked below: (1) the hotbar 'armed spell on item' bridge passes the target and spell ids in swapped order and takes over item use whenever a targeted spell is selected; (2) 272 formula-untargeted spells (war rings, walls, sprays) wrongly require a selected target because untargeted is keyed on the SelfTargeted bit and the wasm isUntargeted reads the wrong field; (3) retail's client-side target-compatibility check (and its messages) is missing entirely, and a server reject with UseDone(None) leaves the predicted windup playing; (4) busy is a time estimate per spell, not retail's outstanding-request counter, so a different-spell recast cuts off the live cast locally while vanilla ACE replies YoureTooBusy; (5) the opt-in component precheck and the spellbook component list use the base formula matched by item name, not the account-personalized formula matched by WCID.
